}}'''Nicholas Charles Handy''' {{postnominals|FRS}}<ref name=frs/> (17 June 1941 – 2 October 2012) was a British theoretical chemist.<ref name="YanaiTew2004">{{cite journal|last1=Yanai|first1=Takeshi|last2=Tew|first2=David P|last3=Handy|first3=Nicholas C|title=A new hybrid exchange–correlation functional using the Coulomb-attenuating method (CAM-B3LYP)|journal=Chemical Physics Letters|volume=393|issue=1–3|year=2004|pages=51–57|issn=0009-2614|doi=10.1016/j.cplett.2004.06.011|bibcode=2004CPL...393...51Y|url=https://zenodo.org/record/1258873}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://announcements.telegraph.co.uk/deaths/154843/handy |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140518180120/http://announcements.telegraph.co.uk/deaths/154843/handy |url-status=dead |archive-date=18 May 2014 |title=Handy - Deaths Announcements - Telegraph Announcements |work=The Daily Telegraph |accessdate=7 October 2012}}</ref> He retired as Professor of [[quantum chemistry]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] in September 2004.<ref name=nch/>

==Education and early life==
Handy was born in [[Wiltshire]], England and educated at [[Clayesmore School]].<ref name="Obit" /> He studied the [[Mathematical Tripos]] at the [[University of Cambridge]]<ref name=ch.cam/> and completed his PhD on theoretical chemistry supervised by [[S. Francis Boys|Samuel Francis Boys]].<ref name=ch.cam/><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Coulson | first1 = C. A. | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.1973.0004 | title = Samuel Francis Boys 1911-1972 | journal = [[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume = 19 | pages = 94–115 | year = 1973 | title-link = S. Francis Boys | doi-access = free }}</ref>

==Research==
Handy wrote 320 scientific papers published in [[physical chemistry|physical]] and [[theoretical chemistry]] journals.<ref name=frs>{{cite journal|last1=Clary|first1=David C.|authorlink1=David Clary|last2=Knowles|first2=Peter J.|last3=Tozer|first3=David J.|title=Nicholas Charles Handy 17 June 1941 – 2 October 2012|journal=[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]]|volume=61|pages=145–160|year=2015|issn=0080-4606|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2015.0002|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=nch>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100228014301/http://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/staff/nch.html|archivedate=28 February 2010|url=http://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/staff/nch.html|title=Professor Nicholas Handy|publisher=University of Cambridge}}</ref><ref name=scopus>{{Scopus|id=7005599042}}</ref>
Handy developed several methods in quantum chemistry and theoretical [[spectroscopy]]. His contributions have helped greatly to the understanding of:
* the transcorrelated method <ref>{{cite journal|journal = The Journal of Chemical Physics
|title = Energies and Expectation Values for Be by the Transcorrelated Method
|last = Handy | first = Nicholas C.
|volume = 51 | issue = 8
| pages =3205–3212 | year = 1999 |doi=10.1063/1.1672496|bibcode = 1969JChPh..51.3205H
}}</ref>
* the long range behaviour of [[Hartree–Fock]] [[molecular orbital|orbitals]]
* semiclassical methods for [[energy level|vibrational energies]]
* the [[variational method (quantum mechanics)|variational method]] for rovibrational wave-functions (in [[normal mode]] and internal coordinates)
* [[Full configuration interaction]] with [[Slater determinant]]s (benchmark studies)
* convergence of the [[Møller–Plesset]] series
* the [[reaction coordinate|reaction path]] [[Hamiltonian (quantum mechanics)|Hamiltonian]]
* [[Anharmonic]] spectroscopic and thermodynamic properties using higher derivative methods
* Brueckner-doubles theory<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Kobayashi |first1=Rika |last2=Handy |first2=Nicholas C. |last3=Amos |first3=Roger D. |last4=Trucks |first4=Gary W. |last5=Frisch |first5=Michael J. |last6=Pople |first6=John A. |title=Gradient theory applied to the Brueckner doubles method |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |date=1991 |volume=95 |issue=9 |pages=6723–6733 |doi=10.1063/1.461544}}</ref>
* [[Open shell]] [[Møller–Plesset]] theory
* frequency-dependent properties 
* [[Density functional theory]] : quadrature, new functionals and molecular properties.

===Awards and honours===
Handy was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1990|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1990]].<ref name=frs/> He was awarded the [[Leverhulme Medal (Royal Society)|Leverhulme Medal]] in 2002<ref name=leverhulme>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150321035351/https://royalsociety.org/awards/leverhulme-medal/|archivedate=21 March 2015|url=http://royalsociety.org/awards/leverhulme-medal/|title=Leverhulme Medal|publisher=Royal Society|accessdate=23 November 2012}}</ref> and was a member of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]].<ref name=iaqms>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140812205923/http://www.iaqms.org/deceased/handy.php|archivedate=12 August 2014|url=http://www.iaqms.org/deceased/handy.php|title=Nicholas Handy at the International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science page}}</ref>

==Death==
On 2 October 2012 Nicholas died after a brief battle with pancreatic cancer.<ref name="Obit">{{cite web |url=http://www.iaqms.org/obituary/NicholasHandyObituary.pdf |title=Nicholas Handy 1941–2012 |last1=Buckingham |first1=David |website= |access-date=28 August 2016 }}</ref>
